content.text:
Durations are in working days: Monday to Friday, except the shaded company holidays. Every link is finish-to-start, and a task starts on the first working day after all of its predecessors finish. Suppose task 4 (Lighting fixtures) takes 4 more working days than planned and nothing else changes. On what date does the project now finish? Answer with the date in the form Fri Mar 5.

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
## Original schedule

Working days exclude weekends and the holidays Thu 11/26, Fri 11/27, Fri 12/25 and Fri 1/1. Tracing the dependencies from the chart:

- Task 1 (Kickoff): Mon 11/16
- Task 2 (Site survey, 3 days): Tue 11/17 to Thu 11/19
- Task 3 (Painting, 7 days, after 2): Fri 11/20 to Wed 12/2
- Task 4 (Lighting fixtures, 6 days, after 3): Thu 12/3 to Thu 12/10
- Task 7 (Ceiling grid, after 1): Tue 11/17 to Tue 11/24
- Task 5 (Deep clean, 7 days, after 4 and 7): Fri 12/11 to Mon 12/21
- Task 6 (Punch list, 6 days, after 5): Tue 12/22 to Wed 12/30
- Task 8 (Flooring, 5 days, after 7): Wed 11/25 to Thu 12/3
- Task 9 (IT cabling, 6 days, after 2 and 8): Fri 12/4 to Fri 12/11
- Task 10 (Handover, after 6 and 9): Thu 12/31

## Delayed schedule

Task 4 now takes 10 working days instead of 6, and nothing else changes.

- Task 4: starts Thu 12/3 and finishes Wed 12/16 (Dec 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 14, 15, 16).
- Task 5 (7 days): starts Thu 12/17. Working days are 17, 18, 21, 22, 23, 24 and Mon 12/28, so it finishes Mon 12/28. Fri 12/25 is a holiday and the weekend is skipped.
- Task 6 (6 days): starts Tue 12/29. Working days are 29, 30, 31, then Mon 1/4, 1/5, 1/6, so it finishes Wed 1/6. Fri 1/1 is a holiday.
- Task 9 finishes Fri 12/11, which is well before task 6, so it does not drive the finish.
- Task 10 (1 day): starts Thu 1/7 and finishes that day.

The project now finishes on Thu Jan 7 (2027).

FINAL ANSWER: Thu Jan 7
